### Task 1 - List of available admonitions used to highlight content used for testing (sample)

::: scenario 
This is a "scenario" admonition that can be used at the beginning of lab guides to provide context about the upcoming tasks. 

It will appear in between dotted lines.
:::

::: note 
This is a "note" admonition for general notes and information. 

It will appear in a "light gray" color.
:::

::: info 
This is a "info" admonition that can be used to provide credentials or information needed for a task.

It will appear in a "light blue" color.
:::

::: tip 
This is a "tip" admonition that can be used for helpful hints or side info.

For example: use it to provide links to useful resources or best practices. 
It will display in "teal" color.
:::

::: hint 
This is a "hint" admonition that can provide subtle guidance during challenging tasks.

For example: "If you can't find the answer, check page 2". 
It will display in a "light violet" color. 
:::

::: caution 
This is a "caution" admonition that can be used for potential pitfalls. 

For example: "Remember to save the value of x, you will need it later". 
It will display in a "yellow" color.
:::

::: warning 
This admonition can be used for important "warnings". 

For example: "While in this lab we are using "all time" in our searches, this is not recommended in a production environment."
It will display in an "orange" color.
:::

::: danger 
This is a "danger" admonition for critical alerts. 

For example: "Do NOT delete or overwrite the x file while copying these files to the new location."
It will appear in a "dark orange" color.
:::



#### Using the "answers" admonition to conceal answers (sample)

The "answers" admonition can be used to conceal answers to questions or challenges you want the learner to discover on their own. 
The format is the same as with other admonitions, but it behaves slightly different. 

```
::: answers 
This content will be concealed from the learner so they can try to find a solution on their own. The answer will still be available so they can validate their results, with or without an instructor.  
:::
```
